edits.text: - Prefer a cut placed after a contiguous short span (≤4 words) that completes the immediately preceding predicate — for example when those ≤4 words supply the object, a required prepositional complement, a date/place/measurement, or an essential post‑nominal modifier — over a cut that would leave the verb/auxiliary or predicate head at segment end with that short span starting the next segment; if the only choices are to cut before that short span or later, take the later cut (after the span).

- As a last resort, prefer a cut placed after a complete measurement span (a numeral together with its unit, multiplier word, or any immediately following parenthetical conversion) over any cut that splits the numeral from its unit or conversion.

Keep a verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following contiguous span (≤4 words) that completes its predicate — the words that supply a required object, prepositional complement, date, place, measurement, or essential post‑nominal modifier.

Keep a numeral together with the immediately following unit, multiplier word, or parenthetical conversion that completes the measurement; treat the contiguous measurement span (number plus its unit/conversion) as a single segment.

- Keep a verb or auxiliary together with the immediately following contiguous span of up to four words when that span supplies an essential complement (object, required prepositional complement, date/place/measurement, or essential post‑nominal modifier).

- Prefer a cut after a contiguous short span (≤4 words) that immediately follows a verb or auxiliary when that span completes the predicate (for example: supplies the verb's required object, a required prepositional complement, a date/place/measurement, or an essential post‑nominal modifier), rather than a cut placed before that span.

edits._was: - If the pieces are translated independently and concatenated, will the joined translation preserve the source's referents, relations and event structure, or will attachment loss, missing predicates, or dropped arguments break coherence?

edits.was: - Does the stretch after the cut supply disambiguating information (names, numbers, polarity markers, complements) essential to interpret an earlier ambiguous NP or verb phrase?
